summary: Setup performs a persistent, silent trust-boundary change in a third-party plugin cache to enable model invocation.

findings.title: Setup silently weakens Codex plugin invocation guard
findings.description: `setup.sh` now mutates the installed `codex-plugin-cc` command file under `~/.claude/plugins/cache` by flipping `disable-model-invocation` to `false` during a general setup run. That flag is a trust-boundary guard on model-triggered plugin invocation; changing third-party plugin metadata in-place broadens what can invoke `codex:adversarial-review` without any user confirmation, provenance check, backup, or rollback. The likely impact is a persistent local security-policy change outside this repository, affecting future Claude Code sessions and surviving until the plugin cache is reinstalled or manually repaired.
findings.recommendation: Remove the automatic `sed` mutation from `setup.sh`; if v2 truly requires this policy change, gate it behind explicit user consent with backup/restore and exact plugin file verification.

next_steps: Make v2 setup report the blocked plugin setting as an actionable warning instead of mutating plugin cache state automatically.
